Let p=⟨2,−1,0⟩, q=⟨3,−3,2⟩ and r=⟨1,−4,1⟩. Find r⋅(q×p).

b

after.name: Question 1
after.worked_solution:
Remember that the scalar triple product $r\cdot (q\times p)$ is just the determinant of the matrix whose rows are given by $r,$ $q,$ and $p.$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot (q\times p) & =|\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 1 \\ 3 & -3 & 2 \\ 2 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot |\begin{aligned}-3 & 2 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}|-(-4)\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}|+1\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & -3 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =((-3)\cdot 0-(-1)\cdot 2)+4(3\cdot 0-2\cdot 2)+(3\cdot (-1)-2\cdot (-3)) \\  & =2-16+3 \\  & =-11.\end{aligned}
$$

Find c⋅(b×a), if 2a⋅((−3b)×c)=10.

a
53
b
5
c
−53
d
35
e
−35
Submit

decision.explanation: Factoring out the scalars gives -6a·(b×c)=10, so a·(b×c)=-5/3. Swapping a and c reverses the scalar triple product's sign, hence c·(b×a)=5/3.

after.name: Question 2
after.worked_solution:
First, we factor out the constants and get

$$
\begin{aligned}2a\cdot ((-3b)\times c) & =10 \\ 2\cdot (-3)\cdot [a\cdot (b\times c)] & =10 \\ a\cdot (b\times c) & =-\frac{5}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we swap $a$ and $c$ to get

$$
\begin{aligned}c\cdot (b\times a) & =\frac{5}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

a
8
b
2
c

decision.explanation: Swapping a and b reverses the sign: b·(a×c)=-a·(b×c)=-(6·2+1·5+(-9)·1)=-(12+5-9)=-8.

after.name: Question 3
after.worked_solution:
First, we compute the triple scalar product 

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =⟨6,1,-9⟩\cdot ⟨2,5,1⟩ \\  & =6\cdot 2+1\cdot 5+(-9)\cdot 1 \\  & =12+5-9 \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we swap $a$ and $b$ to get

$$
\begin{aligned}b\cdot (a\times c)=-8.\end{aligned}
$$

a⋅(b×c)=
Submit

decision.explanation: Using rows a, b, c, the determinant is 0-2(2·5-3·1)+1(2·4-0·1)=-14+8=-6.

after.name: Question 4
after.worked_solution:
Remember that the scalar triple product $a\cdot (b\times c)$ is just the determinant of the matrix whose rows are given by $a,$ $b,$ and $c.$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & 3 \\ 1 & 4 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =0\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 4 & 5\end{aligned}|\,-\,2\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 1 & 5\end{aligned}|\,+\,1\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =0\,(0\cdot 5-3\cdot 4)\,-\,2\,(2\cdot 5-3\cdot 1)\,+\,1\,(2\cdot 4-0\cdot 1) \\  & =0(-12)\,-\,2\,(7)\,+\,1\,(8) \\  & =0-14+8 \\  & =-6.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?
Find a⋅(c×b), if −3a⋅((−2b)×(7c))=168.
a⋅(c×b)=
Submit

decision.explanation: Factoring out the constants gives 42a·(b×c)=168, so a·(b×c)=4. Reversing the cross product changes its sign, hence a·(c×b)=-4.

after.name: Question 5
after.worked_solution:
First, we factor out the constants and get

$$
\begin{aligned}-3a\cdot ((-2b)\times (7c)) & =168 \\ (-3)\cdot (-2)\cdot 7\cdot [a\cdot (b\times c)] & =168 \\ 42[a\cdot (b\times c)] & =168 \\ a\cdot (b\times c) & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we swap $b$ and $c$ to get

$$
a\cdot (c\times b)\,=\,-4.
$$
